text:
Curiously shallow lakes break up the dry plains of Sol’Kesh’s 
western range. A Traveler can wade across these vast expanses 
of water, rarely ever sinking past their full height and when 
in the center of the largest lake, only a haze of cliffs in the east 
reveals more than just endless water from horizon to horizon. 
Both pebbleback auhk and baughur roam in substantial herds in 
these lands, thousands of birds, migrating from across Sol'Kesh 
and even from far distant lands settle in during the spring, while 
nicalliath burst from the shallow silt to claw and rip through 
any creatures foolish enough to step near their chitinous bladed 
forms.
Four Moon
Locations of the Fenlands
Where The Rivers Run
Rapids rush down from the Splitspine mountain peaks, their ice 
cold waters giving this fast flowing river its namesake. While 
home to the most abundant colonies of creekot clams, stepping 
into these near lethal currents will either break a Traveler over 
the countless sharp rocks, or drag them down to the river’s delta 
where rauka aggressively defend the seaweed strewn rivers with 
their monstrously sharp tusks. Coming in from the ocean, silvette 
swim upstream to spawn, their armored bodies slicing through 
the more placid fish, yet falling prey to the lanky fennfistle that 
pluck them from the waters with their long needle-like teeth. 
Sheer cliffs to the north slowly bleed nutrient rich water from the 
marshlands above into the brackish river that stretches between 
the Inmere lake and the eastern ocean. Larkiera, dominate 
the narrow waterways that grow thick with encroaching kelp 
forests, the murky river allowing them to hunt for smaller fish 
and amphibians with ease. Glomunder and wrakis aggressively 
compete for their sliver of muddy sanctuary along the cattail 
covered banks.
Shiverrun
Rhaen
Rushing down from the Splitspine mountain above, the white 
waters of the Mhinfell flow into the crescent bay surrounding 
the Astradale coral island. Cascading waterfalls, stories high, 
exemplify this river with small ambushing lanceleth waiting 
at the base of the waterfalls, their coiled bodies ready to spear 
any ascending spawning fish, or feed on the falling detritus of 
creatures that did not survive the journey. Herds of rauka can be 
found congregating at the river delta that feeds into the crescent 
bay, the mineral rich waters enriching the brackish sea plants 
below and creating a stretch of fertile territory for the aquatic 
beasts to graze and clash over.
Mhinfell
Far within the Tanglewood’s sea of trees rests a sinkhole, its 
surface mirroring the sky above in a perfect mirror of foreboding 
stillness. Within these black waters lie fathomless depths to the 
bedrock of the island, and hosts a large colony of apex predator 
nuthorghull. Well known to devastate larger fauna until they are 
sated and return to their long protracted hibernation. Despite its 
reputation, this large lake feeds the surrounding forest, attracting 
untold number of migrating forest dwellers to its misty edge, its 
clean waters a much needed respite from the endless trees.
Seen as a halfway point from the great expanse of salt water 
surrounding the coral island of Astradale to the Rhaen’s rapids 
that lead to the ocean, this briny lake runs deep. Many of Sol’Kesh’s 
surrounding ocean-bound aquatic creatures traverse the Inmere 
to bypass the northern tip of the island. Nuthorghull, with its thick 
rubbery flesh is able to survive the salty depths and will snatch 
any creatures that enter their deep domain, they nearly meet 
their match with the enormous goliarch that stream past in great 
seasonal migrations. As such a vital path for aquatic creatures, 
many scavengers can be found picking choice carcasses along the 
rivers edge, with scavick, herragath and vinnirex competing in 
voracious confrontations over the freshest kills. 
Rootwell
Inmere
A low lying mist settles over this near endless expanse of swampy Fenlands like a wet shroud, the stink of rotten stagnant water 
permeates the air, while methane rich bubbles rise and pop on the scummy surface. A quiet slurping sound is heard as a solumundis 
drags its body through the thick mud, its long bladed tongue ready to pierce a crimson-winged herragath unawares. Although these 
treacherous bogs are riddled with sinkholes and clouds of incessant biting insects, the glimmering sheen of vigael can be seen on the 
surface’s sluggish waters. Light refracts off the prismatic oil, hinting at its value, as the restorative algae is worth the miles of quagmires 
to reach. While the Mirewynn may look dour at first glance, it is a haven for life as many seabirds feast on the maddening amount of 
insects that breed in the marsh waters that border the salt of the ocean and multitude of streams that bleed from the Tanglewood to the 
north and the cold fresh Shiverrun river to the west. Many of these birds that take roost during the spring bring a much needed respite 
to the herds of baughur and pebbleback auhk, their welcomed beaks enthusiastically picking off parasites and bloodsucking bugs.
Mirewynn
